architect_note: ARCHITECT NOTE (orchestrator, binding under fixer.md step 17). Owning seams: thermal_model.flow_setpoint_for_level with pump_arbiter._flow_target and _flow_inlet_c (mapping), and the objective's level rounding in optimizer.py with its start set (flat zone). Shape: a sliding setpoint scale anchored at measured tank temperature plus a minimum lift, not a better binary choice; the solver scores levels without a zero-slope region below the minimum. coordinator.py should not change (the arbiter has the tank temperature). Optional: count radiator water in the system heat capacity. Controls: flat-price run publishes the same plan; full power still writes the configured ceiling. Mutants to kill: mapping bottom reverted to return temperature; smoothing or new starts dropped (a buffered rounded install with price spread must book above minimum in the cheapest steps, flat unchanged).
brief: On installs whose pump power is set through a heating-flow setpoint behind a buffer tank and mixing valve, the setpoint is a power command (owner, 2026-10-19: a 55 degree setpoint in short slots applies maximum power while the system volume rises slowly). Two defects keep the plan at the minimum level all day despite price spread. (1) flow_setpoint_for_level maps the minimum level to the return temperature (35 C without a return sensor), which on a 23-34 C tank yields about a third of the planned draw. (2) Rounding inside the objective makes cost flat between 0 and the minimum level, so the solver stalls there. Fix: anchor the power-to-setpoint mapping at the measured tank temperature plus a minimum lift, sliding to the configured ceiling at full power; remove the solver flat zone (smooth or duty-cycle scoring of rounded levels, or high-power starts in the cheapest steps). Flat-price null control mandatory: at flat prices the published plan is unchanged and every gain claim is net of the flat-price run. Do not wire draw_range.planned_range into the solve until the mapping is fixed.
